newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Four die in Australian coal mine flood.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Four die in Australian coal mine flood.

text.p: Four Australian coal miners were killed on Thursday when the tunnel they were working in flooded, police said.

The accident at the Gretley colliery in the Hunter Valley north of Sydney occured at about 5.30 a.m. (1830 GMT) when the miners broke through into old works which caused flooding, a police spokesman told Reuters.
Four other miners, some 120 metres underground and about 100 metres from the coalface, were hit by the floodwaters but survived.
"They are lucky to be alive," a spokesman for New South Wales Minerals Minister Bob Martin said. Floodwaters reached one foot from the ceiling of the tunnel, he said.

A total of 42 miners were on the "dogwatch" overnight shift at the colliery, spread over many parts of the big mine which produces 1.3 million tonnes of coal a year. A total of 174 miners work three shifts at the mine.
Rescue workers and investigators on Thursday afternoon were still underground attempting to piece together events which led to the disaster.

The mine in the Hunter Valley, Australia's second largest coal district, is part of extensive coal mining operations controlled by Oakbridge, which is 42-percent owned by the U.S. Cyprus-Amax mining group.
Martin's spokesman said a full government investigation would be conducted into the accident. Oakbridge, which said it did not know the cause of the accident, was conducting its own investigation.
An issue was whether the old diggings were mapped, a spokeswoman for the New South Wales Minerals Council said.
The accident did not rank among Australia's worst coal mining disasters.

The record is held by an explosion in the Mt Kembla mine, south of Sydney, which killed about 100 miners at the turn of the last century. An explosion in the Mt Mulligan mine, Queensland, early this century killed almost as many.
In the last 20 years, an explosion in the Appin mine in NSW killed 14, while explosions in the Moura mine in central Queensland killed 12 in 1986 and 11 in 1994.
